title: Published coefficient/exponent pair (31/10, 1) for the fixed BK/Shoup family

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. claims: For the six-inequality rational LP displayed in proof.md, with u=delta-alpha_I, 0<=alpha_Q<=alpha_I, 0<=alpha_phi<=1/2 and delta>=0, the maximum of u-alpha_phi/2 is 31/10. Its entire maximizing face is alpha_phi=1/5, alpha_Q=9/5, alpha_I=48/5+h and delta=64/5+h for h>=0. In the displayed conservative finite-inequality template, these points yield loss (261/10+2*h)*d+(128/5+2*h), or (783/5+12*h)*n^(4/5)+(517/10+4*h) after the stated dimension substitution. Thus h=0 simultaneously minimizes both loss coefficients within this template at leading coefficient 31/10. This is an arithmetic statement about that LP and template, not an optimality assertion for circuit lower bounds generally.
